From d250bdf531d9cd4096fedbb9f172bb2ca660c868 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Yang Erkun <yangerkun@huawei.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Dec 2025 13:57:06 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] ext4: fix iloc.bh leak in ext4_xattr_inode_update_ref

The error branch for ext4_xattr_inode_update_ref forget to release the
refcount for iloc.bh. Find this when review code.

Fixes: 57295e835408 ("ext4: guard against EA inode refcount underflow in xattr update")
Signed-off-by: Yang Erkun <yangerkun@huawei.com>
Reviewed-by: Baokun Li <libaokun1@huawei.com>
Reviewed-by: Zhang Yi <yi.zhang@huawei.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20251213055706.3417529-1-yangerkun@huawei.com
Signed-off-by: Theodore Ts'o <tytso@mit.edu>
Cc: stable@kernel.org

diff --git a/fs/ext4/xattr.c b/fs/ext4/xattr.c
index 2e02efbddaac..4ed8ddf2a60b 100644
--- a/fs/ext4/xattr.c
+++ b/fs/ext4/xattr.c
@@ -1037,6 +1037,7 @@ static int ext4_xattr_inode_update_ref(handle_t *handle, struct inode *ea_inode,
 		ext4_error_inode(ea_inode, __func__, __LINE__, 0,
 			"EA inode %lu ref wraparound: ref_count=%lld ref_change=%d",
 			ea_inode->i_ino, ref_count, ref_change);
+		brelse(iloc.bh);
 		ret = -EFSCORRUPTED;
 		goto out;
 	}
-- 
2.34.1

### Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes a resource leak in `ext4_xattr_inode_update_ref()` within `fs/ext4/xattr.c`. Specifically, an error handling branch that checks for an extended attribute (EA) inode reference count wraparound fails to release the buffer head `iloc.bh` before jumping to the `out` label, leading to a memory leak. The fix adds a `brelse(iloc.bh)` call to properly release the buffer head before jumping to the error exit.

### Modifications by File

**`fs/ext4/xattr.c`**  
- **Line 1040**: Added `brelse(iloc.bh);` before the `ret = -EFSCORRUPTED; goto out;` statement in the refcount wraparound error path (inside `ext4_xattr_inode_update_ref`).  
- This ensures that `iloc.bh` is always freed when this error condition is encountered, preventing a buffer head leak.

### Relationship of Modifications

The change is a single-line addition in the existing error-handling code. It directly addresses a missing resource release in a specific error condition (refcount wraparound). The `brelse` call matches similar cleanup performed in other error branches within the same function (e.g., after `ext4_xattr_check_block` failures), ensuring consistent resource management. This leak was introduced by commit 57295e835408 ("ext4: guard against EA inode refcount underflow in xattr update").
